facts.fact: 本章是作者 Andrew 于 2012 年与 David E. Cooper 所作的对话；Cooper 是 England Durham University 的 Professor of Philosophy Emeritus，曾任 Aristotelian Society 的 President 及多个 learned societies 的 Chair，著有 A Philosophy of Gardens 与 Convergence with Nature: A Daoist Perspective 两书。
facts.anchor: What follows is a conversation I had with David E. Cooper in 2012.

facts.fact: David 开答：The Ancients 认定善与美之间有 intimate relationship——Greek、Sanskrit、Chinese 等古代语言中译作 “beautiful” 的词在特定语境亦可译作 “good”；而 post-Renaissance 的现代哲学使这层关系 largely disappeared，ethical 与 aesthetic 被当作分离的领域，交叉引入对方考量者会被讥为 pious moralizing 或 “aestheticism”。
facts.anchor: The Ancients certainly thought there was an intimate relationship between the two.

facts.fact: David 阐明古人预告的两条联系：其一，认出并欣赏美（尤其自己不熟悉的美）须 exercise 诸德——impartiality、sympathy、humility，否则无以欣赏 Korean pottery；其二，如 Plato、the Buddha、Kant 等人所言，事物因表达或 exemplify virtue 而被觉美——面容或姿态因显出 compassion 而美，各文化 beauty norms 的差异反映 competing conceptions of the good。
facts.anchor: Second, there’s the idea—voiced by Plato, the Buddha and Kant among others—that things are found beautiful

facts.fact: David 补充一条联系：以 impartiality、humility 等德欣赏美者，其 comportment（faces、speech、gestures）本身即显德而美——故有 beauty in the appreciation of beauty；这使古老的 “the beautiful soul” 观念获得新解：善人之美一在显善的 comportment、face、speech 使其 draw us，二在其乐于欣赏美、attuned to beauty——即 beauty of soul。
facts.anchor: there is, you could say, beauty in the appreciation of beauty

facts.fact: Andrew 举其 philosophy practice 中的三个人为例：P 与 Q 正走在成为 beautiful souls 的路上——voices soft and gentle、faces placid and calm、words simple and direct；第三人 R 虽在把 vase 感知为美时 exercise restraint 与 disinterestedness 之德，却不成为 beautiful soul——Andrew 在其 presence 中不 feel at home，P 亦然，因为 R 不 draw 人。

facts.fact: David 就 R 之案提出两点限定：审美诸德并非德性之全部——具此德者可能 strikingly lacking honesty、courage 等德，dishonesty 等 “vices” 亦会透过 demeanor 显露；且德性通常但非必然 manifest 于 demeanor——R 可能只是 unlucky（如 facial tic，或使其极难表露情感的 “Victorian” upbringing）。
facts.anchor: The case of the third person, R, raises a real issue—one that invites two qualifications

facts.fact: Andrew 赞同 vice（如 arrogance、vanity）可能 tell against virtues 而使 beautiful soul 不可能，继而补出两点：所 exercise 之德须为 salient（humility、simplicity、patience、compassion；manly virtue 属 war 而非审美），且须有 second-order harmony of the virtues；他又转述 P 的 “general attunement to beautiful things” 与 Q 的 “longing for beauty”（P 陷 deep despair 时觉无物为美），David 随即 amend——西方美学之弊在只聚焦对个别对象的判断及其 pleasure，而忽略 “a general way of being in the world”；“longing” 之所以正当，系于 beauty 与 good 的 intimacy。
facts.anchor: the beautiful soul would have to exhibit a second-order harmony of the virtues

facts.fact: 论 transformation：David 引 Plato——真正的教育是灵魂朝 the good and beautiful 的 “turning around”，并借 Iris Murdoch 的 “the fat, relentless ego” 称此转变为 “unselfing”，主张 right friends 与乡野海边之时光；Andrew 以 humbling 开端（承认自己并不真知自己），援引 Aristotle 所谓 “friends of virtue”，并谓 Robinson Crusoe 无 right kind of fellows 则难成 beautiful soul，述 pupil 之德表由 market、society、sport、war 之德移向 openness、sincerity、patience 并终达 delicate harmony；David 再引 Nietzsche——诸德间 oscillate wildly 的生活 lacking in “style”，人生的大任务是 becoming the artist of that life；Andrew 收束：beautiful soul 亦是 exemplar，或身后仅余 tranquil face 与 final words，以此教我们 how to die with lightness and grace。
facts.anchor: Plato wrote that a true education is the “turning around” of a soul in the direction of the good and beautiful
